note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Progressive shortness of breath; no clear trigger or exposure identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Dyspnea gradually worsening over 2 weeks, markedly worse over the last few days.  
  • Now breathless with minimal exertion (walking around the house, to the shops); previously asymptomatic with these activities.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: denied.  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: denied.  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: denied.  
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: not reported.  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing: denied.  
  • Dyspnea: present (progressive).  
  • Swelling distribution (lips/tongue/uvula/face): none; ankle edema noted (non-ENT).  
  • Ear pain/hearing changes, neck pain/swelling: denied.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • Known heart failure; previous similar breathlessness when first diagnosed.  
  • “Small heart attack” ~5 years ago (specific diagnosis not recalled).  
  • No prior emergency injections, ED visits, or hospitalizations for airway issues reported.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergies: none known.  
  • Furosemide – dose/route/frequency not documented (currently 1 tablet daily; plan to double).  
  • Aspirin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Bisoprolol – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social context:
  • Lives alone with two cats (“Polly” and “Tim”).  
  • Works part-time as a lorry driver (day shifts).

Objective:
- Observable swelling: bilateral ankle edema; no facial, lip, tongue, or uvular swelling reported.  
- Airway/breathing: patient speaking in full sentences; no stridor or noisy breathing noted.  
- Mental status: alert and oriented.  
- Vitals and detailed examination findings: Not recorded (clinician stated chest exam, oxygen saturations, and BP were “OK” but no values provided).  
- Others present: none.

Assessment:
- Likely exacerbation of known chronic heart failure causing progressive dyspnea; no evidence of ENT-specific pathology (no throat swelling, stridor, or airway compromise).  
- Justification: gradual onset breathlessness, ankle edema, prior heart failure, absence of ENT obstructive symptoms.

Plan:
- Immediate/treatment actions:
  • Increase Furosemide to “one tablet twice daily” (exact dose not documented).  
  • Arrange blood tests: FBC, renal function.  
  • Arrange echocardiogram within 1–2 weeks.
- Patient instructions:
  • Monitor symptoms closely; remain hydrated as advised for diuretic therapy.  
  • Contact clinic sooner if worsening breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, dizziness, or any new airway symptoms (voice change, throat tightness, stridor).
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  • Call emergency services if severe shortness of breath at rest, syncope, chest pain, or signs of airway compromise develop.
- Follow-up:
  • Review in 1 week to assess response to diuretic dose increase and review test results.  
  • Consider cardiology referral based on echocardiogram findings.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements:
  – Detailed allergy list beyond “none known” (e.g., food, environmental).  
  – Exact doses/routes of all current medications.  
  – Vital signs (HR, BP, RR, SpO₂) and focused ENT/airway examination findings.  
  – Documentation of any auto-injector or anaphylaxis action plan (not relevant but typically reviewed in ENT allergy assessments).  
● Internal conflicts: None identified.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal background noise; occasional connectivity issues but content understandable.
